gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Audio-Technica preamp puts out about 5 dB more line level than the Fluance one: Audio-Technica's manual gives 252 mV for the AT-LP70XBT and Fluance gives 140 mV for the RT81/RT81+. Fluance's own phono and line figures work out to about 31–32 dB of preamp gain, against Audio-Technica's 36 dB.
standout_why: I compared against valveandvinyl.com/turntables/crosley-alternatives, platterandplinth.com/turntables/best-with-preamp, stylusandsound.com/best-turntables-with-built-in-preamp/ and fewbetter.com. fewbetter.com has no turntable content. Valve & Vinyl gives Audio-Technica's 36 dB gain and Fluance's A-weighted and unweighted S/N, but it lists line output as 'Not published' for every model and never works out Fluance's gain. Stylus & Sound gives only the RT81+ 4.0 mV / 140 mV figures, with no Audio-Technica line level and no comparison. Platter & Plinth gives no output, S/N or wow-and-flutter figures for the Audio-Technica or Fluance models. None of them points out that the S/N figures use different weightings.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. Both preamps reach normal consumer line level, so either one drives powered speakers or an AUX input. On the same input, the Audio-Technica plays about 5 dB louder at the same volume setting, so the Fluance may need the volume turned up a bit, especially on low-gain powered speakers. The noise specs can't rank the two directly. Fluance's 67 dB is A-weighted and Audio-Technica's 55 dB has no stated weighting. Fluance's unweighted 60 dB is still above Audio-Technica's >55 dB, but the methods may differ. Neither maker gives a wow-and-flutter method that can be compared: Audio-Technica says <0.25% 'WTD' and Fluance says 0.2% with no method.

findings.label: Phono output level / implied preamp gain
findings.value: 3.5 mV (±3 dB) phono; implied gain ≈ 32.0 dB
findings.source_title: Fluance RT81 Elite High Fidelity Vinyl Turntable
findings.note: Fluance gives no gain figure. Worked out as 20·log10(140/3.5) = 32.0 dB. AT95E cartridge, 2.0 g tracking force, PHONO/LINE switch.

findings.label: Phono output level / implied preamp gain
findings.value: 4.0 mV (±3 dB) phono, 140 mV (-17 dBV) line; implied gain ≈ 30.9 dB
findings.source_title: Fluance RT81+ Elite High Fidelity Vinyl Turntable
findings.note: Worked out as 20·log10(140/4.0) = 30.9 dB, about 5 dB less than Audio-Technica's 36 dB. The page states 'Phono Bypass: Yes, all electronics bypassed when using external preamp'. AT-VM95E cartridge.

findings.label: Signal-to-noise ratio
findings.value: ≥ 67 dB A-weighted, 20 kHz LPF; ≥ 60 dB unweighted, 20 kHz LPF
findings.source_title: Fluance RT81 Elite High Fidelity Vinyl Turntable
findings.note: The RT81+ page gives the same figures. A-weighting raises the number by 7 dB here (67 vs 60). Compare the unweighted 60 dB, not 67, with Audio-Technica's unweighted-or-unstated >55 dB.
